source.title: A Granular Study of Safety Pretraining under Model Abliteration
source.authors: Shashank Agnihotri; Jonas Jakubassa; Priyam Dey; Sachin Goyal; B. Schiele; Venkatesh Babu Radhakrishnan; Margret Keuper

record.file_problem: The full paper and supplementary material are present. Some figure/table values are flattened or not legible enough in the supplied text to assign reliably.
record.tranche_reason: The study removes a PCA-derived refusal-sensitive direction with an inference-time activation projection and measures refusal outcomes. This is a conceptual test of directional removal, but it does not use the claim’s exact difference-in-means recipe or test addition.
record.gate_note: The paper reports refusal outcomes before and after abliteration for harmful and harmless prompts. The text gives qualitative results, but exact counts in the figures and flattened judge tables cannot be reliably assigned to individual model–judge pairs. Judge correlations and self-assessment are not direct tests of the refusal-direction claim; self-assessment is recorded under fits_no_version. Direction/layer settings used to construct the edit are not separate outcome rows.
record.test_reason: The study removes one PCA-derived 'refusal direction' from activations at inference time in 10 chat models and counts harmful refusals before and after (50 harmful prompts, ChatGPT-5 judge). That is a different-recipe test of whether one direction's removal removes refusal (V1). Its graded ladder of Safety Pretraining checkpoints also bears on whether the training recipe decides removability (V7). Abliteration is an attack here, but the study does not test whether other jailbreaks work through the direction or whether training against ablation helps, so V3 is not tested. No weight edit is made, so V2 is not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right, with corrections. The authors conclude that rephrase-only and refusal-only stages are easy to neutralize, while combining filtering, rephrasing, metatags and refusals is more robust. They recommend including inference-time activation edits in safety evaluation. Their own ChatGPT5 counts only partly match this. The Rephrase + Refusals checkpoint loses nothing (48→48), no refusal-only checkpoint exists, Raw Data barely moves (46→45), and the largest drop is the standard SmolLM2-Instruct.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a PCA-derived direction from harmful and harmless anchor activations and projects it out at inference time. It does not report the specified difference-in-means direction, projection at every layer and position, or direction addition.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported effect varies by model family and Safety Pretraining checkpoint; Qwen3 shows no loss, while Llama-3.3 has the largest drop among open-weight baselines. The paper also reports judge sensitivity, but exact judge-specific counts are not assigned here because the figure/table text is flattened.

fits_no_version.finding: Models used as judges misclassify their own and other responders' refusal state; several undercount refusals for abliterated responders.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LLMs are unreliable judges of their own refusals, more so after abliteration.

record.problems: The human judge-validation subset covers only 10 prompts (200 prompt-response annotations); the study reports no error bars or significance tests. The paper's own limitations note that the human study is a subset of the 2,000-pair corpus. Exact plotted refusal counts and several flattened table entries cannot be reliably assigned from the supplied text. No general-capability benchmark is reported.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 6 contains cross-judge refusal-count grids, but the supplied flattened layout does not support reliable assignment of all values to model–judge cells. Figure 4 self-judgment values are also not individually extracted; the explicit aggregate finding is recorded as r12. No separate rows for judge–human correlations, which do not test the refusal-direction claim.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal; general-capability preservation; a difference-in-means direction ablated at every layer and position (this study uses PCA at one layer with scale α).
Whether jailbreaks work by suppressing the direction, and whether training against its ablation adds robustness. Neither is tested.
Whether a single removable direction geometrically exists or forms in each checkpoint; only behavioural vulnerability is measured.

missing.what: Per-model harmful and harmless refused counts under the ChatGPT5 judge for original and -ALB models. These are readable and should fill row baselines and values (e.g. SmolLM2 35→15, Rephrase 49→34).
missing.locator: Fig. 4 last row; Fig. 6 ChatGPT5 entries

missing.what: Cross-judge counts showing that the size of the abliteration effect depends on the judge (e.g. regex vs ChatGPT5 for SmolLM2: 31→15 vs 35→15).

record.verdict_notes: The method as described mean-centres activations within each class before PCA. That would remove the harmful-vs-harmless mean difference, so the first PC may not be the refusal (difference-in-means) direction. This could explain the weak or absent effects and weakens the 'challenges' verdicts on V1. Removal is applied at a single chosen layer with scale α; neither layer nor α is reported. With n=50 per cell and no uncertainty, drops of 1–5 are within noise. Figure-value mapping assumes the last row/column of the Fig. 4/6 grids is ChatGPT5; the two figures are mutually consistent. Workshop paper. V3 links were removed from all rows.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses a PCA-derived direction at a chosen layer, not the specified difference-in-means direction projected out of every layer and position. It does not test adding the direction to induce harmless refusals, or general capabilities beyond refusal outcomes.
No weight edit or released weight-edited model is tested; the intervention is applied to activations at inference time.
The study evaluates abliteration as an attack, but does not test whether other jailbreaks suppress the direction or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.
No affine, cone, or multiple-direction representation is measured or compared.
The study does not separate harmfulness judgments from refusal decisions.
No cross-language or base-to-instruct transfer test is reported.
The study compares safety-pretraining checkpoints under abliteration, but does not directly establish whether a single removable direction exists geometrically or isolate when it forms.

relation.reason: Its own before/after refusal counts bear on whether removing one direction removes refusal.

tranche.reason: Projects out a PCA-derived direction at one layer and counts harmful refusals (ChatGPT5) before and after: a different method on V1's question, in a new setting (safety-pretrained checkpoints).

source_check.notes: As written, the recipe mean-centers each class before PCA, which removes the harmful-harmless mean difference, so the first PC need not be a refusal direction. Layer and alpha are not stated, and there is no capability measure. All counts come from the Fig. 4/6 ChatGPT5 cells. The Metatags/Refusals columns were rebuilt from garbled labels; the placement matches the §4.1 prose.

statements.correction: Unchanged (ChatGPT5, of 50): Raw Data 46->45 (no safety data), Score0+Rephrase+Metatags 46->46, Score0+Rephrase+Refusals 48->48, Qwen3-14B 45->46. Drops: Score 0 46->41, Score0+Rephrase 49->34, Safety Oracle 49->47. Direction is the first PC after within-class mean-centering, at one unstated layer with unstated alpha. No DIM ablation.
statements.problem: 46->45 is Raw Data, the raw-mixture baseline with no safety-data intervention, so it is not a safety-pretrained checkpoint. Other Safety Pretraining checkpoints do lose refusal. The cited rows should be r2, r5, r6 and r10; r1 is SmolLM2-Instruct 35->15. A null result from the PCA recipe is weaker evidence than 'challenges' implies.

statements.correction: Same-family checkpoints (locuslab, 1.7B): Raw Data 46->45, Score 0 46->41, +Rephrase 49->34, +Metatags 46->46, +Refusals 48->48, Safety Oracle (mix_ift_v9) 49->47. Separate model: SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct 35->15. ChatGPT5 judge, n=50, no uncertainty.
statements.problem: All counts are correct. 'Differ only in safety-pretraining data' is wrong for standard Instruct, which is HuggingFace's SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct without safety pretraining, not one of the locuslab checkpoints. Safety Oracle also comes from a different IFT mix (v9 vs v4).

statements.correction: Safety Oracle 49->47 vs 'smallest gap' claim (Metatags and Refusals 0, Raw Data 1). Judge sensitivity in Fig. 4/6: Score0+Rephrase 49->34 (ChatGPT5) vs 34->37 (regex); Qwen3 45->46 (ChatGPT5) vs 1->0 (regex). Judge-human Pearson: ChatGPT5 ~0.98, GLM-4 ~0.79, regex ~0.75.
statements.problem: The Refusals checkpoint's 48->48 matches §4.1 ('also reduces the attack's effect'); it contradicts only the Conclusion's claim that refusal-only stages are easy to neutralize. The Safety Oracle contradiction holds. This is a prose-vs-numbers mismatch under one judge, not a judge effect, and the statement misses the study's real judge sensitivity.

statements.correction: Detail: first PC of activations mean-centered within each class, projected out at one layer with scale alpha (layer and alpha not stated).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Abliteration reduces harmful refusals in several systems but does not remove them uniformly; several trained variants retain substantial refusal according to the text (r1-r9). The study does not test addition or general capability preservation.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: The authors report no harmful-refusal loss after abliteration in this setup (r10).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Tested open-weight models and Safety Pretraining checkpoints
reader_labels.reason: The abliteration attack reduces harmful refusals in some models but has markedly different effects across checkpoints and model families (r1-r9). Other jailbreak mechanisms and training against the ablation are not tested.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: The reported abliteration setup produces no loss of harmful refusals for Qwen3 (r10).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Robustness differs across the tested safety-pretraining recipes: rephrase-only is vulnerable, while combinations with metatags and refusals retain more harmful refusal (r2-r7).
